thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 [P1] Canary alert: release r-2026-03-14 (canary group A) error rate spike detected. 5.2% 5xxs over last 5m (baseline 0.3%). Route: /v1/generate. Canary id: canary-243.
PagerDuty: page fired to alex (oncall) — escalation policy: infra-prod -> sre -> eng-leads.
alex: ack — I'm looking. What changed in this canary?
deploy-bot: rollout r-2026-03-14 started 00:14 UTC. Canary group A: 120 instances, new image tag redwood/inference:2026-03-14-rc3.
maria: saw same metric in dashboards. Also CPU on canary nodes spiked to 95% around 00:18. Might be a bad kernel build or vectorized ops regression.
alex: trying a quick query against the canary logs: `kubectl logs -l canary=canary-243 -n prod --tail 200` — grabbing stderr.
paul: posted a snippet from logs: ```
2026-03-14T00:18:23Z ERROR model-inference: RuntimeError: CUDA OOM on attention kernel shard 2
2026-03-14T00:18:24Z WARN fallback to cpu-kernel for shard 2
2026-03-14T00:18:25Z ERROR grpc: upstream returned 502
```
alex: that looks like memory regression leading to 502s. Is this the quantization patch landed yesterday? Tag shows rc3.
maria: yes, rc3 pulled in a new attention optimization (opt-attn-v2) and switched jemalloc flag. Could be memory fragmentation.
jess: @alex if canary is OOMing, we should pause rollout and roll back canary group. Is there an automated canary pause?
alex: deploy-bot — pause rollout canary-243 and promote rollback for canary group. `deploy-bot pause --canary=canary-243`
deploy-bot: acknowledged. Pausing rollout for canary-243. No further canary promotions will occur.
PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by alex. Escalation paused.
alex: initiating rollback of canary group: `deploy-bot rollback --canary=canary-243 --to-tag=2026-03-13-stable` — executing now.
deploy-bot: rollback started for canary-243. Expected 120 pods to redeploy to tag 2026-03-13-stable; progress 0/120.
paul: monitoring error-rate panel and access logs. Starting to tail /v1/generate 502 responses to capture customer sample ids.
maria: I can open a hotfix branch to revert opt-attn-v2, but let's see rollback impact first. If rollback resolves, hotfix can be delayed.
alex: rolling back completed: 120/120. Post-rollback health checks passing for canary group. Error rate dropped to 0.4% within 3 minutes.
PagerDuty: incident resolved? Need a short postmortem. alex, please hand off to oncall if any followup.
alex: marking incident resolved in PagerDuty, tagging with `canary-rollback`, `regression-opt-attn-v2`. Will start a quick postmortem thread in #incidents-postmortems.
jess: note for postmortem: collect heap/gpu metrics from rc3 nodes, include jemalloc toggle diff, and reproduce under load if possible. Also check autoscaler churn during the spike.
maria: I'll collect kernel/drivers/gpu driver versions across canary vs stable. Also attaching sample request ids: 7d2f4e9c, 7d2f58a1.
paul: customer impact: ~12 customer requests got 502s in the 10m window; none were authenticated enterprise customers, all hosted API keys; reached <0.01% of total traffic.
alex: handoff to night oncall jess for any followups. jess: ack, I'll take it. Adding a temporary suppression rule to alerts for canary groups to avoid noisy repeats during ongoing investigation. :thumbsup:
jess: creating follow-up ticket in JIRA INF-9876: "Investigate opt-attn-v2 memory regression in rc3", assignment: eng-ml + eng-runtime.
alex: thanks team. Closing thread.
(automated) incident-bot: thread closed and archived.
